teaching_contrasts.now: Selecting either numbered option only prepares a local attachment and draft.
teaching_contrasts.why: The operator must see what will travel before choosing Send.
teaching_contrasts.exact: Neither arrival, opening the menu, inspecting Gate, nor staging an attachment invokes a provider. Each consequential send requires a separate operator gesture.

teaching_contrasts.now: Both steps remain visible; selected source files wait until the activation response is admitted.
teaching_contrasts.why: Knowing the second step exists does not authorize it before the first boundary completes.
teaching_contrasts.exact: #2 remains disabled before activation admission. A held or stopped activation cannot unlock it. Local-only bytes never enter either stage.

teaching_contrasts.now: The native conversation carries the governed continuation; its attachments and send stages remain distinct.
teaching_contrasts.why: Physical proximity of files or text does not make them part of the admitted Loom selection.
teaching_contrasts.exact: The handoff begins a fresh native conversation. Earlier conversations and unrelated attachments cannot silently enter the governed request. Ending Loom clears its staged attachments and export authority while retaining the native conversation.

teaching_contrasts.now: Closing an optional menu sends nothing; the transfer still has its declared lifetime.
teaching_contrasts.why: A person may pause or exit, but a pause cannot quietly extend custody or resurrect expired material.
teaching_contrasts.exact: Closing inspection or the step menu is not Send. Expiry requires a fresh origin handoff. A passing synthetic practice route cannot certify penalty-free resumable rest after expiry.

teaching_contrasts.now: A failed new attempt does not replace the last admitted continuation.
teaching_contrasts.why: An export must describe the current governed work rather than the latest text that happened to appear nearby.
teaching_contrasts.exact: Export remains bound to the admitted continuation and its lineage. Ordinary chat, failed requests, and fabricated prior answers cannot acquire admitted-result authority.

teaching_contrasts.now: The #1 acknowledgment proves the activation stage completed; it is not the source-bearing prior Loom answer.
teaching_contrasts.why: A stage receipt answers which governed step actually happened. A content predecessor answers which admitted work the next continuation may rely on. Collapsing them would either leak source-derived content into #1 or let a handshake masquerade as substantive prior work.
teaching_contrasts.exact: The activation carries only a commitment to any origin prior result. #2 presents the selected source bytes and may present that committed source-bearing result. Later continuations must match the immediately preceding admitted continuation result while separately carrying its stage receipt.

teaching_contrasts.now: A local binding check can compare selected bytes without calling a provider.
teaching_contrasts.why: A finite check is useful precisely because its scope is bounded.
teaching_contrasts.exact: A file-binding receipt is not universal semantic enforcement, adversarial field efficacy, physical tomography, Golden Egg evidence, provider quality, or release authority.
